admission.justification: The former conditional trigger and card-writer exception were real prior choices; replacing them constrains every later operational memory route.

alternatives.option: Refuse ordinary legacy operations regardless of converted memory elsewhere; retain only the named reads and conversion/recovery routes.
alternatives.reason: The build cannot infer operational support from a local conversion census, and a single format boundary prevents ungated legacy publication.

alternatives.option: Retain the conditional trigger and card-writer exception until a converted branch or worktree is observed.
alternatives.reason: It leaves never-converted repositories operating on the unsupported old format and makes local sibling state decide admission.
alternatives.reconsider_when: A separate developer decision deliberately restores ordinary legacy-format support with an explicit validated publication contract.

consequences: The location probe supplies recovery wording only.
Card writes require converted memory; citation_migrate and memory-citations --migrate are unregistered.
Converted/converting/crossing routes retain their existing validation and transaction owners.
context: The prior cutover-window trigger admitted never-converted repositories and exempted card writers. That could continue legacy operation without an invariant gate; MIK-R46 under D39(b)/D47 requires conversion first.
decider: Developer D39(b)/D47, approved MIK-R46@v2 rules 1, 2 and 5.

evidence: requirements/MIK-R46-v2-conversion-precedes-ordinary-memory-operations.md under D39(b)/D47; rule 7 rejects retire when this master lands.
